passages.title: Confined Space Entry
passages.text:
A confined space is any area large enough for a worker to enter and perform tasks, but which has limited or restricted means of entry and exit and is not designed for continuous occupancy. Common examples on a job site include storage tanks, sewers, manholes, pipelines, silos, and pits. Because of their enclosed shape, these spaces can trap hazards that would dissipate harmlessly in the open air.

Not all confined spaces carry the same level of danger. Regulators distinguish between a non-permit confined space and a permit-required confined space. A permit-required space, often shortened to permit space, has one or more serious hazards: a hazardous atmosphere, a material that could engulf an entrant, an inward-sloping or tapering design that could trap a person, or any other recognized serious safety threat. Before anyone enters a permit space, an employer must issue a written entry permit that documents the precautions taken and the conditions allowed.

The most frequent killer in confined spaces is the atmosphere itself. Oxygen can be displaced by other gases, leaving too little to breathe, or it can be enriched to a level that makes a fire spread violently. Toxic vapors such as hydrogen sulfide may accumulate, and flammable gases can reach explosive concentrations. For this reason, the air must be tested with a calibrated gas monitor before entry and continuously while work proceeds. Testing follows a set order: oxygen first, then flammable gases, then toxic contaminants.

A safe entry depends on assigned roles. The authorized entrant performs the work inside. The attendant remains stationed outside, maintains constant communication with the entrant, monitors conditions, and never enters to attempt a rescue without proper equipment and backup. The entry supervisor authorizes the permit, verifies that all precautions are in place, and terminates entry when the job is done or conditions change. Ventilation equipment is frequently used to supply fresh air and dilute contaminants.

Rescue planning is mandatory before entry begins, not improvised afterward. A disturbing share of confined-space fatalities are would-be rescuers who rushed in without protection and were overcome by the same hazard that felled the first victim. Effective rescue relies on retrieval lines, harnesses, and trained teams who can extract an entrant without becoming casualties themselves.

passages.title: Lockout/Tagout
passages.text:
Lockout/tagout, commonly abbreviated LOTO, is a safety procedure used to ensure that dangerous machines are properly shut off and cannot be started again before maintenance or repair work is finished. The hazard it guards against is the unexpected release of energy. When a machine is being serviced, an unplanned startup or the sudden discharge of stored energy can crush, cut, burn, or electrocute the worker performing the task.

Energy comes in many forms, and a thorough procedure must address all of them. Electrical energy is the most familiar, but mechanical, hydraulic, pneumatic, chemical, thermal, and gravitational energy can be just as deadly. A raised hydraulic arm, for example, stores gravitational energy that can drop without warning if its supply is simply switched off. Stored or residual energy must therefore be released, blocked, or otherwise rendered safe, not merely disconnected.

The two terms in the name describe two different controls. A lockout uses a physical lock to hold an energy-isolating device, such as a breaker or valve, in the safe position so it cannot be moved. A tagout uses a prominent warning tag attached to that device to alert others that it must not be operated. A lockout is generally considered more protective because a lock physically prevents operation, whereas a tag only communicates a warning and can be ignored or removed.

A cornerstone of the procedure is that each authorized worker applies his or her own lock and keeps the only key. This rule means no one else can re-energize the equipment while that worker is still exposed. When several people work on the same machine, each attaches an individual lock, often using a group lockout device, so the machine cannot be restored until every worker has removed his or her own lock.

A standard sequence brings these principles together: notify affected employees, shut the equipment down through its normal stopping procedure, isolate it from every energy source, apply locks and tags, release or restrain any stored energy, and finally verify isolation by attempting to operate the controls. Only after the controls confirm a zero-energy state does work begin. Restoring the equipment reverses these steps, with a careful check that all tools are clear and all guards are replaced.

passages.title: Fall Protection and the Personal Fall Arrest System
passages.text:
Falls remain one of the leading causes of serious injury and death on construction and industrial sites. Under OSHA 29 CFR 1926.501, fall protection is required whenever a worker on a construction site is exposed to a fall of six feet or more to a lower level; some general-industry settings set the trigger at four feet. The most common approach is the personal fall arrest system, often abbreviated PFAS. A complete PFAS has three working parts: an anchorage, a body harness, and a connecting device such as a lanyard or self-retracting lifeline. Workers sometimes remember these parts with the phrase "the ABCs of fall protection" — anchorage, body wear, and connector.

The anchorage is the fixed point to which the system attaches. Per 29 CFR 1926.502(d)(15), an anchorage used for fall arrest must support at least 5,000 pounds per attached worker, OR be designed, installed, and used as part of a complete PFAS that maintains a safety factor of at least two under the supervision of a qualified person. Selecting a weak or improvised anchor, such as a piece of conduit or a small pipe, is a frequent and dangerous error. Anchor PLACEMENT also matters: an anchor set far to one side of the worker can produce a swing fall, in which the worker pendulums sideways into a wall or other obstacle, so anchors should be positioned as directly above the work area as the structure allows.

The full-body harness distributes the force of a fall across the thighs, pelvis, chest, and shoulders rather than concentrating it on a single area. Older body belts, which wrapped only the waist, are no longer permitted for fall arrest because they can cause internal injury or allow a worker to slip out entirely. The harness should fit snugly, and the dorsal D-ring — the attachment point on the back — should sit between the shoulder blades.

The connector links the harness to the anchorage. A shock-absorbing lanyard contains a tear-away pack that deploys during a fall to reduce the arresting force on the body. Because such a lanyard can extend several feet as it deploys, calculating total fall clearance is essential. Workers must account for the lanyard length, the deceleration distance, the height of the worker, and a safety margin so the body does not strike a lower level before the system stops the fall.

Equipment must be inspected before each use. Frayed webbing, corroded hardware, deployed shock packs, and missing labels are all grounds for removing a component from service. Under 1926.502(d)(20), any PFAS component subjected to impact loading must be IMMEDIATELY REMOVED FROM SERVICE and not reused for employee protection until a competent person inspects it and determines that it is undamaged and suitable for reuse. Some employers choose to retire impacted equipment as company policy, but the standard itself requires removal-pending-inspection rather than automatic retirement.

passages.title: Electrical Safety and the Role of Grounding
passages.text:
Electricity is essential to nearly every jobsite, but it is also a hidden hazard that can injure or kill in a fraction of a second. Because the human body conducts electricity, even a relatively small current passing through the body can disrupt the heart's rhythm. As little as 100 milliamperes can be fatal, far below the level needed to power a common hand drill. For this reason, electrical safety relies on engineered protections rather than on a worker's caution alone.

Grounding is one of the most important of these protections. Grounding provides a low-resistance path that allows stray electrical current to flow safely into the earth instead of through a person. In a properly grounded tool, the metal housing is connected to a third prong on the plug. If a wire inside the tool comes loose and contacts the housing, the current travels through the ground path and trips the circuit breaker rather than energizing the case and waiting for a worker to touch it. A tool with a broken or removed ground prong loses this protection entirely, which is why cutting off the third prong to fit an older outlet is strictly prohibited.

Grounding works hand in hand with the ground-fault circuit interrupter, or GFCI. A GFCI constantly compares the current flowing out on the hot wire with the current returning on the neutral wire. If even a small difference appears — meaning some current is escaping along an unintended path, possibly through a person — the GFCI cuts power within milliseconds. GFCIs are required on construction sites for receptacles that are not part of the permanent wiring and are especially critical in wet or damp locations, where the body's resistance drops and shock becomes more likely.

Double-insulated tools offer an alternative approach. Instead of relying on a ground wire, they enclose their electrical parts in two independent layers of insulation, so a single failure cannot energize any part a worker might touch. Such tools carry a square-within-a-square symbol and use a two-prong plug.

Before using any cord or tool, a worker should inspect it for cracked insulation, exposed conductors, and damaged plugs. Defective equipment must be tagged and removed from service. These simple habits, combined with engineered safeguards, dramatically reduce the risk of electrical injury.

questions.question: The drawing shows a 15 kg sandbag and a 30 kg sandbag dropped from the same crane height at the same moment. Ignoring air resistance, which sandbag accelerates downward faster?
choices: Both accelerate downward at the same rate
questions.explanation: Free-fall acceleration g is the same for all masses, so both sandbags accelerate downward at the same rate and reach the ground together.

questions.question: In the figure, a board 18 ft long is set against a 9 ft high truck bed to form a ramp. Compared with lifting the load straight up, the ramp requires how much force (ignoring friction)?
questions.explanation: MA = 18/9 = 2, so the ramp cuts the needed force in half compared with a straight vertical lift.

questions.question: The drawing shows two race cars rounding the same circular turn, finishing the turn together. Car 1 is on the inner line and Car 2 is on the outer line. Which car covered MORE distance during the turn?
choices: Both covered exactly the same distance
questions.explanation: The outer line is a larger-radius arc, so it is physically longer. Car 2 on the outside therefore covers more distance than Car 1 on the inside through the same turn.

questions.question: In the drawing, two pistons of EQUAL area (4 cm² each) are joined by hydraulic fluid. When you push on one piston, how does the force on the other piston compare?
questions.explanation: Force equals pressure times area, and the pressure is equal throughout the fluid. Because the two pistons have the same area, they exert the same force on each other.

questions.question: The figure shows a heavy 600 lb load hung from a block-and-tackle with three supporting rope segments. The effort required to hold it is approximately:
questions.explanation: Three supporting rope segments give MA = 3. Effort = 600 / 3 = 200 lb.

questions.question: In the figure a 1 kg block and a 10 kg block are dropped together from a rooftop of equal height. Neglecting air resistance, what happens?
choices: Both blocks hit the ground together
The 10 kg block hits first because it is heavier
The 1 kg block hits first because it is lighter
questions.explanation: Free-fall acceleration is the same for every mass, so dropping the blocks from the same height makes them land simultaneously. Mass does not affect the time to fall.

questions.question: In the drawing, a barrel is raised with a lever. Which arrangement lets a small child lift the barrel?
choices: Long bar with the fulcrum near the barrel
Short bar with the fulcrum near the child
A bar with no fulcrum at all
questions.explanation: A long effort arm plus a fulcrum near the load both reduce the force needed. This arrangement lets even a small child lift the barrel.

questions.question: In the drawing, a hydraulic system has a small piston of 3 square centimeters and a large piston of 9 square centimeters filled with the same fluid. Which piston produces the greater output force?
questions.explanation: Because the pressure is identical throughout the connected fluid, force equals pressure times area. The 9 sq cm piston has 3 times the area of the 3 sq cm piston, so it produces 3 times the force.

questions.question: The drawing shows a small 14 cm pulley and a large 28 cm pulley sharing one open belt. To make the large 28 cm pulley spin as FAST as possible, the operator should:
choices: Drive it from the smaller 14 cm pulley
Drive it from an even larger pulley
questions.explanation: Output speed is proportional to (driver diameter) / (driven diameter). To make the 28 cm driven pulley spin faster, use a LARGER driver pulley — that ratio rises above 1.0 so the output spins faster than the driver. Driving it from the 14 cm pulley makes the 28 cm pulley spin at only half the driver's speed; crossing the belt only reverses direction.

questions.question: In the drawing, where is the fluid PRESSURE the lowest?
questions.explanation: The fluid speeds up in the narrow section. Faster-moving fluid has lower pressure, so pressure is lowest at the small right end.

questions.question: In the drawing, the fulcrum is near the right end, the box sits left of it, and the effort is applied at the far left. Is lifting the box easier or harder than if the effort and load were equal distances from the fulcrum?
choices: Harder, since the effort arm is shorter than the load arm
Easier, since the effort arm is longer than the load arm
questions.explanation: The effort arm (fulcrum to far left) is longer than the load arm (fulcrum to box). A longer effort arm means less force, so it is easier.

questions.question: Two batteries of the same size power identical bulbs. Which arrangement will drain its battery FASTER?
choices: Both drain the battery at the same rate
questions.explanation: The parallel arrangement draws more total current from the battery because its total resistance is lower. Drawing more current uses up the battery's stored energy faster.

questions.question: Which everyday tool is NOT an example of a wedge?
questions.explanation: Axes and chisels are wedges; a pulley is a different simple machine.

questions.question: In the figure, a beam rests on supports A (left) and B (right). The 300 lb engine block sits much closer to support A. Which support carries the greater share of the weight?
questions.explanation: The 300 lb engine block is only 3 ft from support A but 9 ft from support B, so A is much closer to the load. The support nearer the load carries the larger share — reaction at A = dRight / (dLeft + dRight) = 9/12 = 75 percent of the total weight.

questions.question: Which best explains why rubber soles grip a rough sidewalk well?
choices: Rubber removes friction from the sidewalk
High friction between rubber and rough surface
questions.explanation: Friction between rubber and a rough surface is high, providing grip.

questions.question: The figure shows a hydraulic press with two connected pistons. The left piston has a face area of 2 square inches and the right piston has a face area of 8 square inches. The same fluid fills both cylinders. Which piston pushes out with MORE force?
choices: Both push with exactly the same force
questions.explanation: By Pascal's principle the pressure is equal throughout the fluid, and force equals pressure times area. The larger 8 sq in piston has 4 times the area of the 2 sq in piston, so it exerts the greater force.

questions.question: The figure shows a wheelchair ramp 20 ft long rising 5 ft. A load that weighs 200 lb is pushed up at steady speed. Ignoring friction, about how much force is needed along the ramp?
questions.explanation: MA = length/height = 20/5 = 4. Required force = weight / MA = 200 / 4 = 50 lb.

questions.question: In the drawing, two meshed gears each have 15 teeth and the left gear turns counterclockwise. Which way does the right gear turn?
questions.explanation: Meshed gears rotate in opposite directions regardless of size. The left gear turns counterclockwise, so the right gear turns clockwise.

questions.question: A doorstop is an example of a wedge that:
choices: Removes friction between the door and floor
Converts a horizontal door push into a strong wedging force against the floor
questions.explanation: The doorstop wedge converts the door's small horizontal force into a large normal force that resists motion.

questions.question: In the drawing, two identical weights hang from springs P and Q. Spring P stretches 8 cm and spring Q stretches 11 cm. If both weights are pulled down and released, which one will spring back up faster?
choices: Both return at the same speed
questions.explanation: Equal weights stretch the stiffer spring less, so P (8 cm) is stiffer than Q (11 cm). A stiffer spring exerts a stronger restoring force, so the weight on P springs back faster.

questions.question: Two solid balls of equal size — one foam, one steel — are held completely submerged at the same depth in water. Compared to each other, the buoyant forces on the two balls are:
choices: Equal, because they displace the same volume of water
Greater on the foam ball because it would float
Zero on the steel ball because it would sink
questions.explanation: Archimedes' principle: buoyant force equals the weight of the displaced fluid. Two objects of equal volume held fully submerged at the same depth displace the same volume, so the buoyant force is equal on both. Weight is what differs — steel is denser than foam, so its WEIGHT exceeds the buoyant force and it would sink if released; foam's weight is less than the buoyant force so it would rise. But while held submerged, buoyant force is identical.

questions.question: When a bus accelerates from a stop, a standing passenger feels pushed backward because:
choices: The bus floor pushes the passenger backward
The body tends to stay at rest while the bus moves forward
questions.explanation: Inertia keeps the passenger at rest as the bus accelerates beneath them, giving the sensation of being pushed back.

questions.question: In the figure, a 24-tooth gear drives a 48-tooth gear. If the small gear turns counterclockwise, which way does the large gear turn?
questions.explanation: Meshed gears turn opposite directions. The driver turns counterclockwise, so the driven gear turns clockwise.

questions.question: The figure compares two fulcrum positions for lifting the same load. Position 1 has the fulcrum near the load; Position 2 has the fulcrum near the middle. Which position requires less effort?
questions.explanation: A fulcrum nearer the load shortens the load arm and lengthens the effort arm, reducing the force needed. Position 1 is easier.

questions.question: Why are the handles of electrical tools usually covered in plastic or rubber rather than bare metal?
choices: Plastic increases the tool's power output
Plastic conducts electricity better than metal
Plastic insulates the user from electric current
questions.explanation: Plastic and rubber are insulators, protecting the user from electric shock.

questions.question: The drawing shows two equal 20 cm pulleys joined by a belt. Compared with the driver, the driven pulley turns:
questions.explanation: Belt speed depends on pulley size. When both pulleys are the same diameter (20 cm and 20 cm), neither is smaller, so they turn at the same speed.

questions.question: Three identical bulbs are connected in parallel to a battery. How does each bulb's brightness compare to the same three bulbs wired in series?
choices: Brightness is the same in both circuits
questions.explanation: In parallel, each bulb gets the full battery voltage, so all three glow brightly. In series, the voltage is split three ways, making each bulb much dimmer.

questions.question: An ice cube floats and a rock sinks in the same pool. This is because:
choices: Ice is less dense than water; rock is denser
Ice is colder than the water
questions.explanation: Density relative to water determines whether an object floats or sinks.

questions.question: A doorknob is an example of a wheel-and-axle because:
choices: The large knob turns a smaller shaft with more force
It eliminates friction in the latch
questions.explanation: The knob (wheel) magnifies the hand's force to turn the latch shaft (axle).

questions.question: In the figure, an 18-tooth gear meshes with a 54-tooth gear. To make the small gear turn three times, the large gear must turn:
questions.explanation: The ratio is 54 to 18, or 3 to 1. The small gear turns 3 times for every 1 turn of the large gear, so one turn of the large gear gives three of the small.

questions.question: The figure shows two different-looking springs, each carrying the same hanging weight. Both springs stretch exactly 7 cm. What can you conclude about their stiffness?
questions.explanation: With equal weights, stretch depends only on stiffness. Both springs stretch the same 7 cm, so they must have equal stiffness regardless of appearance.

questions.question: Two points X and Y are at the same depth in a connected water tank of irregular shape. The pressure at X compared to Y is:
questions.explanation: At equal depths in a connected static fluid, pressure is equal regardless of container shape.

questions.question: In a wheel-and-axle, force is typically applied to the wheel because:
choices: Turning the larger wheel multiplies force at the axle
The axle is harder to grip
questions.explanation: The larger radius gives greater torque, so a small effort on the wheel becomes a large force on the axle.

questions.question: The figure shows a worker on the ground using a single fixed pulley mounted high on a wall to raise a 180 lb beam. Compared with lifting the beam by hand with no pulley, the fixed pulley:
choices: Lets him pull with much less force
Lets him pull downward instead of lifting up, but with the same force
questions.explanation: A fixed pulley changes only the direction of effort (he can pull down instead of up). The force needed is still equal to the 180 lb load.

questions.question: The drawing shows a 10 ft ramp rising 2 ft. A person pushes with 30 lb of force to slide an object up at constant speed. Ignoring friction, how heavy is the object?
questions.explanation: MA = 10/2 = 5. Weight = force * MA = 30 * 5 = 150 lb.

questions.question: A weightlifter holds a heavy barbell motionless overhead. While holding it still, the work being done on the barbell is:
questions.explanation: Although the lifter exerts force, the barbell does not move, so no work is done on it.

questions.question: Identical boxes receive the same push on ice and on asphalt. Which box slides farther?
questions.explanation: Lower friction on ice lets the box keep sliding farther for the same applied push.

questions.question: Three bulbs are connected to a battery. Which arrangement draws the MOST total current from the battery?
choices: Total current is the same either way
questions.explanation: Adding bulbs in parallel lowers the total resistance because it creates more paths for current. Lower total resistance means the battery delivers more total current than the same bulbs wired in series.

questions.question: An empty capped bottle floats, but the same bottle filled with sand sinks. What changed?
choices: The average density of the bottle increased above water's
questions.explanation: Adding sand raises the overall density above that of water, so it sinks.

questions.question: Why are dams typically built thicker at the bottom than at the top?
choices: Water pressure is much greater at the bottom
Concrete is weaker at the top
questions.explanation: Pressure increases with depth, so the dam must resist greater force near its base.

questions.question: Why is the blade of a wood-splitting axe shaped as a wedge?
choices: To direct force outward and split the wood
questions.explanation: The wedge shape converts downward swing force into sideways splitting force on the wood fibers.

questions.question: Water flows through this pipe from X to Y. Where is the water moving faster?
questions.explanation: By continuity, when cross-sectional area decreases, fluid speed must increase. The narrow end (Y) has higher velocity.

questions.question: The figure shows a single pulley bolted to an overhead beam, with the rope passing over it so a worker pulls straight down to raise a 120 lb crate. About how much force must the worker pull with?
questions.explanation: A single fixed pulley only changes the direction of the force; it gives no mechanical advantage (MA = 1). Effort = load = 120 lb.

questions.question: In which setup will the bulb light when each rod is placed in the circuit?
questions.explanation: Aluminum is a metal and conducts; glass is an insulator.

questions.question: What is the main idea of the passage?
choices: Confined spaces are always illegal to enter without a permit
Confined spaces present serious, often atmospheric, hazards that require classification, testing, defined roles, and rescue planning before entry
Storage tanks and silos are the only true confined spaces
Ventilation equipment eliminates all confined-space dangers
questions.explanation: The passage broadly covers what confined spaces are, how they are classified, the hazards (especially atmospheric), the assigned roles, and rescue planning. Choice B captures this scope, while the others are too narrow or contradicted by the text.

questions.question: According to the passage, what document must an employer issue before a worker enters a permit-required confined space?
questions.explanation: The passage states that before anyone enters a permit space, an employer must issue a written entry permit documenting precautions and allowed conditions.

questions.question: In what order does the passage say the atmosphere must be tested?
choices: Toxic contaminants, oxygen, then flammable gases
Flammable gases, toxic contaminants, then oxygen
Oxygen, flammable gases, then toxic contaminants
Oxygen, toxic contaminants, then flammable gases
questions.explanation: The passage explicitly states the order: oxygen first, then flammable gases, then toxic contaminants.

questions.question: As used in the passage, the word "dissipate" most nearly means
questions.explanation: The passage contrasts hazards being trapped in an enclosed space versus dissipating harmlessly in open air, indicating that 'dissipate' means to spread out and disperse.

questions.question: Based on the passage, why does the attendant remain outside the space?
choices: Because the attendant is not trained to do any work
To monitor conditions and maintain communication while avoiding entering without proper equipment and backup
Because only one person is legally allowed near a permit space
To issue the entry permit from outside
questions.explanation: The passage says the attendant stays outside, maintains constant communication, monitors conditions, and never enters to attempt a rescue without proper equipment and backup. This supports inferring the protective reason for staying outside.

questions.question: Which choice would make the BEST title for the passage?
choices: Safe Entry Into Confined Spaces: Permits, Testing, and Rescue
How to Become a Confined-Space Attendant
questions.explanation: The passage centers on permit vs non-permit spaces, atmospheric testing, attendants, and rescue equipment — all elements of safe confined-space entry.

questions.question: All of the following are supported by the passage EXCEPT:
choices: An attendant must remain outside the space during entry
Atmospheric testing must be performed before entry
Oxygen levels must fall within a safe range
A permit is never required for any confined space
questions.explanation: The passage distinguishes permit-required from non-permit spaces, so it does NOT support the claim that permits are never required.

questions.question: According to the passage, which step must occur FIRST?
choices: Entrants begin work inside the space
The atmosphere is tested for oxygen and hazards
The attendant leaves the entry point
questions.explanation: Atmospheric testing must precede entry, before workers may enter the space.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of lockout/tagout, according to the passage?
choices: To ensure dangerous machines are shut off and cannot restart or release energy before service work is finished
To label which machines are newest
To reduce a company's electricity costs
questions.explanation: The passage opens by stating LOTO ensures dangerous machines are properly shut off and cannot be started again, guarding against the unexpected release of energy during service.

questions.question: Which of the following is given as an example of stored gravitational energy?
choices: A raised hydraulic arm that can drop
questions.explanation: The passage uses a raised hydraulic arm as an example of stored gravitational energy that can drop without warning if its supply is switched off.

questions.question: Why does the passage state that a lockout is generally more protective than a tagout?
choices: A lock is cheaper than a tag
A lock physically prevents operation, while a tag only warns and can be ignored or removed
A tag cannot be seen from a distance
questions.explanation: The passage explains a lockout physically prevents operation, whereas a tag only communicates a warning that can be ignored or removed, making lockout more protective.

questions.question: As used in the passage, the word "residual" most nearly means
questions.explanation: The phrase 'stored or residual energy must therefore be released' uses 'residual' to mean energy that remains or is left over in the system, which must still be made safe.

questions.question: Based on the passage, why must each worker apply his or her own lock and keep the only key?
choices: So the supervisor can track attendance
So no one else can re-energize the equipment while that worker is still exposed
So the machine runs more efficiently afterward
So the tag does not need to be used
questions.explanation: The passage states this rule ensures no one else can re-energize the equipment while that worker is still exposed, which is the inferred safety reason.

questions.question: Of the following titles, which one most accurately captures what the passage is about?
choices: How to Repair Broken Equipment Quickly
Why Tags Are Better Than Locks
questions.explanation: The passage centers on the LOTO procedure as a worker-protection method that isolates a machine's energy source before maintenance.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT mentioned in the passage as part of the lockout/tagout procedure?
choices: Applying both a lock and a tag
Verifying that the machine has zero energy
questions.explanation: The passage describes isolating, locking, tagging, and verifying zero energy, but never requires notifying the manufacturer.

questions.question: Based on the passage, if a worker skipped the step of verifying zero energy before beginning maintenance, the most likely result would be:
choices: A workplace injury caused by unexpected energy release
A delay in completing the maintenance task on time
A fine issued by the equipment's manufacturer
The lock being unable to attach to the energy source
questions.explanation: The passage identifies failure to follow LOTO as a leading cause of workplace injuries; skipping zero-energy verification most directly risks injury.

questions.question: What is the main idea of the passage?
choices: Body belts are safer than full-body harnesses
A personal fall arrest system has several components that must be correctly selected, used, and inspected to prevent falls
Falls are rare on most construction sites
Anchorages are the only important part of fall protection
questions.explanation: The passage describes the parts of a PFAS and stresses correct selection, use, and inspection of each, which is the central point. The other options are either contradicted by the text or address only a single detail.

questions.question: According to the passage, what is the minimum load an anchorage must support per attached worker when not designed by a qualified person?
questions.explanation: The passage states a reliable anchorage must support at least 5,000 pounds per attached worker, unless designed by a qualified person to a safety factor of at least two.

questions.question: What do the "ABCs of fall protection" stand for?
questions.explanation: The passage explicitly defines the ABCs as anchorage, body wear, and connector.

questions.question: According to the passage, what must happen to a harness that has been subjected to impact loading from a fall arrest?
choices: It must be removed from service until a competent person inspects it and determines it is undamaged and suitable for reuse
It must be destroyed by burning
It must be passed to another worker
questions.explanation: Under OSHA 1926.502(d)(20) (cited in the passage), any PFAS component subjected to impact loading must be removed from service and may only return to service after competent-person inspection. Automatic destruction is not the standard requirement.

questions.question: As used in the passage, the word "deploys" most nearly means:
choices: activates and extends to do its job
questions.explanation: In context, the shock-absorbing lanyard's tear-away pack "deploys" during a fall to reduce arresting force, meaning it activates and extends to function. The other options contradict the protective purpose described.

questions.question: Which choice would make the BEST title for the passage?
choices: A Climber's Guide to Mountaineering Gear
PFAS: Components and Use of Personal Fall Arrest Systems
The History of OSHA's General Industry Rules
Avoiding All Work Above Ground Level
questions.explanation: The passage focuses on the components and proper use of a personal fall arrest system.

questions.question: All of the following are supported by the passage EXCEPT:
choices: A body harness distributes arrest forces over the torso
Swing fall is a hazard to consider when choosing an anchor
Lanyards and SRLs must be inspected before use
Fall protection is required only at heights above 25 feet in construction
questions.explanation: The passage names 6 feet as the construction trigger, not 25 feet, so D is unsupported. Each of the other choices is supported: A (harness distributes force across the torso), B (swing fall is now explicitly noted as an anchor-placement hazard), and C (lanyards and SRLs must be inspected).

questions.question: Which sentence BEST summarizes the passage?
choices: Fall arrest systems are no longer required on most job sites.
OSHA only enforces fall protection in general industry, not construction.
Body harnesses have replaced all other safety equipment.
A complete PFAS pairs an anchor, body harness, and connector, and must be inspected and rigged to limit arrest forces and swing falls.
questions.explanation: This captures the three PFAS parts (ABCs), the inspection requirement, the deceleration / fall clearance considerations, and the swing-fall placement hazard described in the passage.

questions.question: What is the central idea of this passage?

Double-insulated tools should never be used
Engineered protections such as grounding and GFCIs, along with inspection habits, reduce the danger of electrical work
Only electricians can be injured by electricity
questions.explanation: The passage explains the electrical hazard and then describes grounding, GFCIs, double insulation, and inspection as protections — the central idea is that these safeguards reduce risk.

questions.question: According to the passage, how does grounding protect a worker?

By providing a low-resistance path for stray current to flow into the earth instead of through a person
By eliminating the need for circuit breakers
questions.explanation: The passage states grounding provides a low-resistance path allowing stray current to flow safely into the earth rather than through a person.

questions.question: How does a GFCI determine that current may be escaping along an unintended path?
choices: It measures the temperature of the wire
It listens for a humming sound
It compares the current on the hot wire with the current returning on the neutral wire and detects a difference
It checks the color of the insulation
questions.explanation: The passage explains a GFCI compares outgoing current on the hot wire to returning current on the neutral wire and cuts power if a difference appears.

questions.question: Why is cutting off the third prong of a tool's plug strictly prohibited?
choices: It makes the tool harder to store
It removes the ground path and eliminates that protection entirely
It voids the tool's color coding
questions.explanation: The passage states a tool with a broken or removed ground prong loses the grounding protection entirely, so cutting off the prong is prohibited.

questions.question: As used in the passage, the word "conducts" most nearly means:
choices: carries or allows the flow of electricity
questions.explanation: In context, the human body "conducts electricity," meaning it carries or allows the flow of electrical current. The other meanings do not fit this scientific usage.

questions.question: Which choice would make the BEST title for the passage?
choices: How to Wire a Residential Panel
Grounding, GFCIs, and Safe Work Around Electricity
questions.explanation: The passage centers on grounding, GFCIs, double-insulated tools, and clearances — all electrical-safety topics.

questions.question: According to the passage, what is the direct consequence of a ground fault when a GFCI is present?
choices: The tool runs hotter than normal
The GFCI trips and cuts power quickly
questions.explanation: GFCIs sense imbalance from a ground fault and trip to interrupt current before serious shock occurs.

questions.question: With which statement would the author most likely agree?
choices: Working clearances around energized equipment can be ignored if you are careful
Double-insulated tools eliminate the need for any electrical caution
GFCI protection is especially important in wet or damp locations
Grounding is unnecessary on modern equipment
questions.explanation: The passage specifically emphasizes wet-location safety and GFCI use.

passages.title: Curing Concrete: Keeping Moisture In
passages.text:
Curing is the process of maintaining adequate moisture and a favorable temperature in freshly placed concrete so that it can develop its full strength and durability. Many people assume concrete "dries" to become hard, but this is a misunderstanding. Concrete hardens through a chemical reaction called hydration, in which cement reacts with water. If the water evaporates too quickly, hydration stops before it is complete, and the concrete never reaches the strength the mix was designed to deliver.

The early days after placement are the most critical. A common rule on the job site is that the first seven days largely determine the final quality of the slab. Concrete that is properly cured for seven days can reach roughly 70 percent of its designed strength, while concrete left to dry on its own may reach far less. Premature drying at the surface also leads to defects such as dusting, scaling, and surface cracking, all of which weaken the finished product.

Several methods are used to retain moisture during curing. Workers may pond water on flat slabs, cover the surface with wet burlap or cotton mats, or apply a continuous fine mist. Another approach is to seal the moisture inside by covering the concrete with plastic sheeting or by spraying on a liquid membrane-forming compound that forms a film over the surface. Each method has the same goal: to slow evaporation so that enough water remains for hydration to continue.

Temperature matters as well. Hydration slows dramatically in cold weather and may stop entirely if the concrete freezes before it gains sufficient strength. In hot, dry, or windy conditions, evaporation accelerates, and crews must take extra steps to protect the surface. For this reason, curing is not a single action but an ongoing process of monitoring and protection.

Skipping or shortening the curing period is a costly mistake. The added strength and resistance to wear gained from proper curing far outweigh the small expense of water, coverings, or labor. A slab that fails early because it was allowed to dry too fast must often be removed and replaced, whereas a well-cured slab serves reliably for decades. Understanding that curing controls a chemical reaction, rather than simply drying the material, is the key to producing concrete that performs as intended.

passages.title: Reading Blueprints and Symbols
passages.text:
A blueprint is a scaled drawing that communicates exactly how a structure or system is to be built. Because a drawing cannot show every object at its true size, blueprints are produced to scale, meaning that a small measurement on paper represents a larger real-world distance. A common architectural scale, for example, is one-quarter inch on the drawing equal to one foot of actual length. Reading the scale correctly is essential, because measuring a line and assuming it is full size would lead to serious errors.

Blueprints rely on standardized symbols rather than words so that drawings stay compact and can be understood across trades. A small rectangle interrupted by a gap may indicate a door, while a thin double line can represent a window set into a wall. Electrical drawings use their own set of symbols: a circle with lines radiating from it may stand for a ceiling light, and an S often marks a switch. Because these symbols are not always obvious, every set of plans includes a legend, sometimes called a key, that lists each symbol and explains what it represents. A worker who is unsure of a marking should consult the legend rather than guess.

Lines themselves carry meaning. A solid line usually shows an edge or surface that is visible, while a dashed or hidden line represents an object located behind or beneath another, such as a footing under a wall. Center lines, dimension lines, and break lines each follow their own conventions. Dimension lines are especially important because they state the exact measurements between points, removing the need to scale the drawing by hand whenever a printed figure is provided.

Most building plans are organized into several sheets. A plan view looks straight down from above, as if the roof were removed, and is used to show the layout of rooms or equipment. An elevation view shows a structure from the side, revealing height and exterior features. A section view shows what a cut through the structure would reveal, exposing interior details that other views hide.

Notes and a title block round out a typical sheet. The title block, usually in a corner, identifies the project, the drawing number, the scale, and the date or revision. Whenever a written dimension and a scaled measurement disagree, the written dimension governs. By combining scale, symbols, line types, views, and notes, a blueprint gives the crew a complete and reliable guide to the work.

passages.title: Hand and Power Tool Safety
passages.text:
Hand and power tools are among the most common pieces of equipment on any job site, and they are also a frequent source of injury. The hazards usually fall into a few predictable categories: being struck by a flying object, being cut by a sharp edge, being caught in moving parts, and being exposed to harmful dust, fumes, or vibration. Because these tools are used so routinely, workers can become careless, and most tool-related injuries trace back to misuse, poor maintenance, or a missing guard rather than to a defect in the tool itself.

The foundation of safe hand-tool use is keeping tools in good condition. A wrench with worn jaws can slip and cause a fall; a chisel with a mushroomed head can throw metal fragments when struck; a screwdriver used as a pry bar may snap. Workers should inspect tools before each use, remove damaged tools from service, and tag them so no one picks them up by mistake. Cutting tools must be kept sharp, since a dull blade requires more force and is more likely to slip. Workpieces must also be secured by clamps or a vise rather than held by hand, because if the workpiece shifts under a powered cutting tool the operator can experience kickback and lose control.

Power tools introduce additional hazards because of their speed and energy. Every power tool that can do so should be fitted with a guard that shields the operator from the point of operation, rotating parts, and flying chips. Guards must never be removed or tied back to make a job go faster. Electric tools should be grounded or double-insulated; damaged cords must be replaced rather than taped. For 120-volt, single-phase, 15- and 20-ampere receptacles that are NOT part of the permanent wiring of a construction site, OSHA 29 CFR 1926.404(b)(1) requires either ground-fault circuit-interrupter (GFCI) protection on all such outlets used by employees, OR an assured equipment-grounding-conductor program covering cord sets and plug-connected equipment. Before changing a blade or bit, the operator should disconnect the tool from its power source, because an accidental start can cause a serious laceration or amputation.

Personal protective equipment is the last line of defense. Safety glasses or a face shield protect against flying particles, hearing protection guards against the high noise levels many power tools produce, and gloves protect the hands — though gloves should be avoided around rotating bits that could catch the fabric and pull the hand in. Loose clothing, jewelry, and long hair present the same entanglement risk and must be secured.

Finally, the work area itself matters. Cluttered floors, poor lighting, and wet conditions all raise the chance of an accident. By combining well-maintained tools, intact guards, appropriate protective equipment, secured workpieces, and a clean workspace, employers and workers can prevent the great majority of tool-related injuries.

passages.title: OSHA Recordkeeping
passages.text:
The Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) requires many employers to keep records of serious work-related injuries and illnesses. The purpose of this recordkeeping is not to assign blame but to track patterns, identify hazards, and give both employers and regulators reliable data for improving workplace safety. Accurate records help a company see where its injuries are concentrated and decide where to focus its prevention efforts.

Not every employer must keep these records. Businesses with ten or fewer employees during the previous calendar year are generally exempt from routine recordkeeping, as are establishments classified in certain lower-hazard industries such as some retail and office settings. However, all covered employers, regardless of size or industry, must still report the most severe events directly to OSHA: any work-related fatality must be reported within eight hours, and any work-related inpatient hospitalization, amputation, or loss of an eye must be reported within twenty-four hours.

Employers who are required to keep records use a standard set of forms. The OSHA 300 Log is used to record each recordable injury or illness as it occurs, listing details such as the employee's job, the date, and the nature of the case. The OSHA 301 Incident Report provides additional detail about each individual case. At the end of the year, the employer prepares the OSHA 300A Summary, which totals the year's cases. The 300A Summary must be posted in a visible location in the workplace from February 1 through April 30 of the following year, even if no injuries occurred during the year.

An injury or illness is generally considered recordable if it is work-related and results in death, days away from work, restricted work or job transfer, medical treatment beyond first aid, or loss of consciousness. Minor cases treated with only first aid—such as a small bandage or an over-the-counter pain reliever—do not have to be recorded.

Records must be retained for five years following the end of the calendar year they cover, and during that period the employer must update the logs if it learns of a recordable case it missed. Employees and their representatives have the right to review these records. By maintaining honest and complete records, employers create a clear picture of workplace safety that benefits workers, management, and regulators alike.

questions.question: In the figure two 6 kg bricks are let go from the top of a wall at the same height and same instant. Which brick is moving faster just before it hits the ground?
choices: They have the same speed at impact
questions.explanation: Both bricks accelerate at the same rate g over the same fall distance, so they reach the same final speed and hit the ground together.

questions.question: In the figure, a transformer sits on a beam two thirds of the way toward support B (right). Which support bears the heavier reaction?
questions.explanation: The transformer is 8 ft from A but only 4 ft from B. The nearer support, B, carries the larger reaction. Reaction at B = 8/12 = about 67 percent.

questions.question: The drawing shows three ramps that all rise to the same 4 ft height but have different slope lengths: 8 ft, 12 ft, and 20 ft. Up which ramp does a cart roll up MOST easily?
questions.explanation: To the same height, the longest ramp is the gentlest and gives the greatest mechanical advantage, so the 20 ft ramp is easiest.

questions.question: Three bulbs are wired in series with a battery. What is true about the current flowing through each bulb?
choices: The same current flows through every bulb
The first bulb gets more current than the last
Each bulb draws its own separate current
questions.explanation: In a series circuit there is only one path for current, so the identical current flows through every component in the loop, including each bulb.

questions.question: The drawing shows two springs, A and B, each holding an identical weight. Spring A stretches 4 cm and spring B stretches 9 cm. Which spring is stiffer?
questions.explanation: Equal weights hang from both springs, so the spring that stretches LESS is stiffer. Spring A stretches only 4 cm versus 9 cm for B, so Spring A is stiffer.

questions.question: In the figure, a worker pries up a heavy rock with a bar resting on a fulcrum. To lift the rock with the LEAST force, where should the worker push?
choices: At the far end of the bar, away from the fulcrum
At the same spot as the rock
questions.explanation: Pushing at the far end gives the longest effort arm. A longer effort arm means less force is needed, so the far end requires the least force.

questions.question: In the drawing, a two-rope block-and-tackle supports a 360 lb load. What effort is needed to hold it?
questions.explanation: Two supporting ropes give MA = 2. Effort = 360 / 2 = 180 lb.

questions.question: In a series circuit with three bulbs and a battery, where in the loop is the current the strongest?
choices: The current is the same everywhere in the loop
It is strongest right after the battery
It is strongest at the last bulb
questions.explanation: A series circuit is a single path, so the current has the same value at every point around the loop. Current is not 'used up' as it passes through the bulbs.

questions.question: In the figure, three pulley setups lift the same 270 lb load: A has 1 supporting rope, B has 2 supporting ropes, C has 3 supporting ropes. The setup shown for THIS problem has 2 supporting ropes. The effort it needs is:
questions.explanation: With 2 supporting ropes the mechanical advantage is 2. Effort = 270 / 2 = 135 lb. (More ropes would reduce the force further.)

questions.question: The figure shows two ramps of equal 9 ft length: Ramp A reaches a 3 ft ledge, Ramp B reaches a 9 ft ledge. Which ramp lets you move the load up with LESS force?
questions.explanation: For equal length, the ramp to the lower height is gentler. Ramp A: MA = 9/3 = 3; Ramp B: MA = 9/9 = 1. Higher MA means less force, so Ramp A is easier.

questions.question: In the figure, a block-and-tackle uses two supporting rope segments to lift a 300 lb engine. The effort force on the free rope end is about:
questions.explanation: Two supporting rope segments give MA = 2. Effort = 300 / 2 = 150 lb.

questions.question: Why do hiking boots have deeply patterned tread on the soles?
choices: The tread reduces the boot weight
The tread increases friction by grabbing into rough surfaces
The tread keeps water out of the boot interior
questions.explanation: Patterned tread interlocks with the irregularities of rough terrain, increasing the effective friction so the boot grips better.

questions.question: Two bars lift the same log. In the drawing, Bar A has its effort applied far from the fulcrum and Bar B has its effort applied close to the fulcrum. Which bar makes lifting easier?
questions.explanation: A longer effort arm requires less force. Bar A, with effort applied farther from the fulcrum, makes lifting easier.

questions.question: The drawing shows two identical 5 kg spheres released from the same shelf height at the same moment. Which sphere strikes the floor sooner?
questions.explanation: Both spheres have the same mass and fall the same distance with the same acceleration g. They reach the floor at the same time.

questions.question: In the drawing, three meshed gears (30, 20, 40 teeth) are in a row. The 30-tooth gear turns clockwise. Which way does the 40-tooth gear turn?
questions.explanation: Direction alternates: 30-tooth CW, 20-tooth CCW, 40-tooth CW. The 20-tooth gear is just an idler, so the last gear matches the first.

questions.question: The drawing shows a 40 cm pulley driving a 16 cm pulley with an open belt. Which statement matches the figure?
choices: The 16 cm pulley turns slower and the opposite direction
The 16 cm pulley turns faster and the same direction
Both pulleys turn at the same speed and direction
questions.explanation: An open belt keeps both pulleys turning the same direction, and the smaller pulley turns faster. The 16 cm pulley is smaller, so it turns faster in the same direction.

questions.question: A diver swims from point P down to point Q. What happens to the water pressure on the diver?
questions.explanation: Pressure rises as depth increases due to additional water weight above.

questions.question: In the drawing, the narrow piston has an area of 1 square inch and the wide piston has an area of 12 square inches. On which piston does the fluid produce the larger total force?
choices: The total force is the same on each
questions.explanation: Pascal's principle keeps the pressure equal everywhere in the fluid, and force equals that pressure times area. The 12 sq in piston has 12 times the area, so the fluid pushes it with 12 times the force.

questions.question: A sealed empty metal can floats, but the same can with the lid removed fills with water and sinks. Why?
choices: Once water enters, the can's average density exceeds water's
questions.explanation: Trapping air keeps average density low; filling with water makes it denser than the surrounding water.

questions.question: In the figure two horses gallop around a curved track and cross the same finish line at the same moment. Horse A runs along the inside rail; Horse B runs in the lane farther out. Which horse needed the greater speed?
choices: They needed identical speeds since they tied
Horse A, on the inside rail
Horse B, in the outer lane
questions.explanation: Even in a tie, the outer lane is a longer arc. Horse B traveled a greater distance in the same time, so Horse B had to run at a greater speed than Horse A.

questions.question: In the figure, a CROSSED belt links a 12 cm pulley turning counterclockwise to a 36 cm pulley. Which way does the 36 cm pulley turn?
questions.explanation: A crossed belt reverses rotation. Since the driver turns counterclockwise, the crossed belt makes the driven pulley turn the opposite way: clockwise.

questions.question: The figure shows spring 1 stretched 20 cm and spring 2 stretched 10 cm, each holding the same hanging mass. About how does the stiffness of spring 2 compare to spring 1?
choices: Spring 2 is about twice as stiff
Spring 2 is about half as stiff
questions.explanation: For equal weights, stiffness is inversely related to stretch. Spring 2 stretches half as much (10 cm versus 20 cm), so it must be about twice as stiff.

questions.question: In the figure, a 10-tooth gear meshes with a 40-tooth gear. Which gear spins faster?
choices: Both spin at the same speed
questions.explanation: The gear with fewer teeth turns faster. The 10-tooth gear makes more revolutions than the 40-tooth gear, so it spins faster.

questions.question: In the figure, a large 36-tooth gear drives a small 12-tooth gear. Compared to the large gear, the small gear turns:
questions.explanation: Fewer teeth means faster rotation. The 12-tooth gear spins faster than the 36-tooth gear it meshes with.

questions.question: In the figure an 8 kg can and a 100 kg drum are released from the same height at the same time. Neglecting air resistance, which lands first?
choices: They land at the same time
questions.explanation: Despite the large weight difference, both objects fall with the same acceleration g. Released from the same height, the can and the drum land at the same time.

questions.question: Compared to a wide wedge, a very narrow wedge:
choices: Splits material more easily but requires more strokes
Splits with less force per stroke but in fewer strokes
questions.explanation: Narrower wedges have greater mechanical advantage but must travel farther, so more strokes are needed.

questions.question: Two hockey pucks are given identical flicks: one slides on polished ice, the other on rubber matting. Which travels farther?
choices: The one on rubber, since rubber provides more push
They travel the same distance because they were flicked equally
The one on ice, because friction is lower
questions.explanation: Lower friction on ice means less force decelerating the puck, so it slides farther for the same initial push.

questions.question: The figure shows a brake system where the master piston is 5 square millimeters and the slave piston is 20 square millimeters. Which piston applies the GREATER clamping force?
questions.explanation: The hydraulic pressure is the same at both pistons, so the larger area gives the larger force. The 20 sq mm piston has 4 times the area and therefore 4 times the force of the 5 sq mm piston.

questions.question: Why does a steering wheel let a driver turn the front wheels with far less hand force than gripping the steering shaft directly?
choices: A hidden pulley inside the column multiplies force
The large wheel turning a small shaft multiplies the driver's applied force
The wheel reduces the weight of the shaft
questions.explanation: A steering wheel is a wheel-and-axle: applying a small force over a large radius produces a much larger force at the smaller-radius shaft.

questions.question: A circuit is tested with a rubber block and then a wood block as the connector. The bulb:
choices: Does not light in either case
Lights only with the rubber block
Lights only with the wood block
questions.explanation: Both rubber and dry wood are insulators, so no current flows in either circuit.

questions.question: In the drawing, where would a tiny floating bead drift along MOST SLOWLY?
choices: It drifts at the same rate everywhere
questions.explanation: Fluid is slowest where the pipe is widest. A bead carried by the fluid drifts slowest in the large reservoir end.

questions.question: Water flows steadily through a pipe whose cross-section varies along its length. Where does the water move SLOWEST?
choices: Speed is the same throughout for steady flow
questions.explanation: The continuity equation A·v = constant means a larger cross-sectional area gives a smaller flow velocity, so the widest section has the slowest water.

questions.question: A box slides across a frictionless level floor at constant speed. The net work done on the box is:
questions.explanation: With no net force and constant velocity, the net work on the box is zero.

questions.question: Oil flows through the pipe shown in the figure. Where does the oil move SLOWER?
choices: The speed is identical at both ends
questions.explanation: As the pipe widens, the same volume of oil spreads through a larger area, so it slows down. The oil moves slower at the wide finish.

questions.question: A mechanic places the fulcrum just 0.5 ft from a heavy engine block and applies effort 4 ft away. Compared to a setup where both distances were equal, the required effort is:
questions.explanation: Mechanical advantage = 4/0.5 = 8, so effort drops to 1/8 of the load.

questions.question: When a car brakes hard, an unbelted passenger lurches forward into the dashboard. The cause is best described as:
choices: Air pressure inside the car pushing the passenger forward
Inertia — the body keeps moving while the car slows beneath it
Gravity briefly tipping forward as the car decelerates
questions.explanation: An object in motion stays in motion unless acted on by a force; when the car decelerates, nothing initially decelerates the passenger, so they continue forward.

questions.question: In the drawing, a flag is being raised on a pole using one pulley attached to the top of the pole. As the worker pulls the rope DOWNWARD, the flag moves:
questions.explanation: A fixed pulley reverses the direction of the applied force. Pulling the rope down makes the load (the flag) rise.

questions.question: A roofer hoists a 90 kg bundle of shingles using a single fixed pulley anchored to a beam. What is the mechanical advantage of this setup?
questions.explanation: A single fixed pulley only redirects the rope — it does not multiply force. The mechanical advantage equals 1.

questions.question: A cork floats while a penny sinks. Which statement is correct?
choices: The cork is less dense than water; the penny is denser
The penny weighs less than the cork
Buoyant force only acts on metals
questions.explanation: Float/sink depends on density relative to the fluid.

questions.question: Two ramps reach the same height. Ramp 1 is 10 ft long and Ramp 2 is 20 ft long. Compared to Ramp 1, pushing a box up Ramp 2 requires:
choices: Half the force over twice the distance
Twice the force over half the distance
The same force over the same distance
questions.explanation: Doubling the ramp length at the same height halves the input force but doubles the push distance. The work done is the same.

questions.question: Which simple-machine family includes a knife blade, an axe head, and a chisel?
questions.explanation: Knives, axes, and chisels all convert a small input force into a larger splitting force over a short distance — the defining trade-off of a wedge.

questions.question: A worker pushes hard against a heavy crate, but the crate does not move. The mechanical work done ON the crate is:
choices: Equal to the worker's force × the time spent pushing
Zero, because work requires the load to move some distance
questions.explanation: Work in physics equals force × distance moved in the direction of force. No motion means no mechanical work, regardless of how long the force is applied.

questions.question: A worker uses a hand crank with a 12-inch handle radius to turn a drum with a 2-inch radius. The setup gives a mechanical advantage because:
choices: The drum spins faster than the crank
The crank radius is larger than the drum radius, multiplying force at the drum
The cable winding on the drum makes it stronger
questions.explanation: A wheel-and-axle multiplies force by the ratio of radii: 12 / 2 = 6× force on the drum compared with the hand at the crank.

questions.question: An electrician working on a live circuit prefers a screwdriver with a plastic-coated handle because:
choices: The plastic prevents current from flowing through the user
The plastic makes the screwdriver lighter
The plastic conducts electricity safely to ground
questions.explanation: Plastic is an insulator and protects the user from electrical shock.

questions.question: What is the main idea of the passage?
choices: Concrete becomes hard only after all of its water has evaporated.
Proper curing maintains moisture so concrete can fully develop its strength through hydration.
Cold weather is the single greatest threat to finished concrete.
Plastic sheeting is the only reliable way to cure a concrete slab.
questions.explanation: The passage repeatedly stresses that curing maintains moisture and temperature so hydration can complete and concrete reaches full strength; this is the central point. The other choices are either contradicted (drying) or are minor details (cold weather, plastic sheeting).

questions.question: According to the passage, concrete hardens primarily because of what process?
choices: A chemical reaction called hydration between cement and water
questions.explanation: The passage states directly that "concrete hardens through a chemical reaction called hydration, in which cement reacts with water."

questions.question: Roughly what percentage of its designed strength can concrete reach when properly cured for seven days?
questions.explanation: The passage states that concrete properly cured for seven days "can reach roughly 70 percent of its designed strength."

questions.question: In the passage, the word "hydration" most nearly means
choices: The drying out of a material
The chemical reaction between cement and water
The cooling of concrete in cold weather
The application of a sealing film to the surface
questions.explanation: The passage defines hydration as the reaction "in which cement reacts with water," so in context it refers to that chemical reaction, not drying or cooling.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT listed in the passage as a method for retaining moisture during curing?
choices: Covering the surface with wet burlap or cotton mats
Spraying on a liquid membrane-forming compound
Heating the concrete with open flames
questions.explanation: Ponding, wet burlap/mats, misting, plastic sheeting, and membrane-forming compounds are all listed. Heating with open flames is never mentioned as a moisture-retention method.

questions.question: Which alternative title would best fit the passage?
choices: Why Concrete Needs Moisture to Gain Strength
questions.explanation: The passage explains that concrete cures through hydration and that retaining moisture for about seven days allows it to develop most of its strength.

questions.question: Which item is NOT listed in the passage as a method for keeping moisture in curing concrete?
questions.explanation: The passage lists wet burlap, sprinklers, ponding, plastic sheeting, and curing compounds; heated air blowers are not mentioned and would dry the surface.

questions.question: The passage most strongly implies that the author believes:
choices: The first seven days of curing are critical to a concrete pour's long-term strength
Concrete should be kept completely dry while it cures
Curing compounds are inferior to all other moisture-retention methods
Freezing temperatures have no effect on curing concrete
questions.explanation: The passage stresses that concrete reaches 65-75% of its 28-day strength in the first week and that moisture must be maintained then, implying the author views that window as critical.

questions.question: What is the central idea of the passage?
choices: Blueprints are decorative drawings with little practical use
A title block is the only feature a worker needs to read a plan
Electrical symbols are the only important part of a blueprint
Blueprints use scale, symbols, line types, views, and notes to communicate exactly how to build something
questions.explanation: The passage describes how scale, symbols, line types, views, and notes work together to communicate construction information, and the closing sentence summarizes exactly this. The other options focus on single details or contradict the text.

questions.question: According to the passage, what does a dashed or hidden line on a blueprint represent?
choices: The exact measurement between two points
An object located behind or beneath another
The boundary of the title block
questions.explanation: The passage states that "a dashed or hidden line represents an object located behind or beneath another, such as a footing under a wall."

questions.question: Why are blueprints drawn to scale?
choices: Because a drawing cannot show every object at its true size
Because color printing is too expensive
Because symbols cannot be used on full-size drawings
questions.explanation: The passage explains that "a drawing cannot show every object at its true size," so blueprints are produced to scale where a small measurement represents a larger real distance.

questions.question: In the passage, the word "legend" most nearly means
choices: A famous story about a building
A list that explains what each symbol represents
questions.explanation: The passage defines the legend, "sometimes called a key," as a list that "lists each symbol and explains what it represents."

questions.question: Based on the passage, what should a worker do when unsure about a symbol on the plans?
choices: Measure the symbol with a scale
questions.explanation: The passage states that "a worker who is unsure of a marking should consult the legend rather than guess."

questions.question: Which choice would make the BEST title for the passage?
choices: Understanding Plan Symbols, Scales, and Revisions
questions.explanation: The passage focuses on scale, standardized symbols, line types, views, dimensions, notes, and the title block — the essentials of reading blueprints. The other options miss the central topic.

questions.question: With which statement would the author most likely agree?
choices: Revision clouds should be ignored on the field set
Electrical and plumbing symbols are interchangeable
Scale should be confirmed before measuring dimensions on a print
Sections and elevations show the same view
questions.explanation: The passage emphasizes scales and accurate reading; checking scale before measuring is consistent with its guidance.

questions.question: Which sentence BEST summarizes the passage?
choices: Blueprints use standardized scale, symbols, line types, views, dimensions, and a title block to communicate construction information across trades.
Blueprints are decorative drawings without standardized meaning.
Revisions are tracked only in writing, not on drawings.
Plumbing and electrical work do not appear on drawings.
questions.explanation: This statement captures the topics the passage actually teaches: scale, symbols, line types, views, dimensions/notes, and the title block. The other summaries are contradicted by or unsupported in the passage.

questions.question: What is the main idea of the passage?
choices: Power tools are inherently more dangerous than hand tools and should be avoided
Personal protective equipment alone is enough to keep workers safe
Most tool-related injuries can be prevented through proper maintenance, guarding, protective equipment, and a clean work area
Tool defects are the leading cause of job-site injuries
questions.explanation: The passage states that most injuries trace back to misuse and poor practices, and concludes that combining maintained tools, guards, PPE, and a clean workspace prevents the majority of injuries. This is the central point, not any single detail.

questions.question: According to the passage, what does a 'mushroomed head' on a chisel cause when the chisel is struck?
choices: The chisel to bend out of shape
questions.explanation: The passage specifically says a chisel with a mushroomed head 'can throw metal fragments when struck.'

questions.question: Why should an operator disconnect a power tool from its power source before changing a blade or bit?
choices: To save electricity while the tool is idle
Because an accidental start can cause a serious laceration or amputation
To allow the motor to cool down
questions.explanation: The passage directly states the tool should be disconnected 'because an accidental start can cause a serious laceration or amputation.'

questions.question: It can be inferred from the passage that a worker who removes a guard to work faster is most likely to:
choices: Improve the quality of the finished work
Reduce noise levels produced by the tool
Extend the life of the power tool
Increase the risk of being struck by flying chips or caught in rotating parts
questions.explanation: The passage says guards shield the operator from the point of operation, rotating parts, and flying chips, and warns they must never be removed. Removing one therefore reasonably increases exposure to exactly those hazards, even though the passage does not state this consequence word-for-word.

questions.question: As used in the passage, the phrase 'last line of defense' most nearly means that personal protective equipment:
choices: Is the first thing a worker should rely on
Is the protection that remains after other safeguards, used as a final barrier
Is only needed for power tools
Replaces the need to maintain tools
questions.explanation: In context, PPE is described after maintenance and guarding, and 'last line of defense' signals it is the final barrier relied on once other measures are in place—not the primary safeguard.

questions.question: All of the following are supported by the passage EXCEPT:
choices: Guards on power tools should remain in place during use
Either GFCI protection or an assured equipment-grounding-conductor program must be used on covered construction-site receptacles
Eye and ear PPE may be needed depending on the tool
Removing a tool guard is acceptable to speed up the cut
questions.explanation: The passage stresses keeping guards in place, so removing them (D) is contradicted. The other three options are directly supported: guards in place (A), the GFCI-or-AEGC requirement for covered receptacles (B), and choosing PPE based on the tool type (C).

questions.question: According to the passage, what can directly result if a workpiece is held by hand instead of secured by a clamp or vise during a powered cut?
questions.explanation: The passage states that an unsecured workpiece can shift under a powered cutting tool, causing kickback and loss of control. The other options are unrelated to the hazard discussed.

questions.question: With which statement would the author most likely agree?
choices: Pre-use inspection of tools prevents many injuries
Double-insulated tools never require any electrical precautions
Eye protection is optional for grinding
Guards slow workers down and should be removed
questions.explanation: Inspection is highlighted as part of safe tool use throughout the passage.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of OSHA recordkeeping, according to the passage?
choices: To assign blame to employers for unsafe conditions
To track patterns, identify hazards, and provide reliable data for improving safety
To determine how much each employer must pay in fines
To rank companies against their competitors
questions.explanation: The passage states the purpose 'is not to assign blame but to track patterns, identify hazards, and give both employers and regulators reliable data for improving workplace safety.'

questions.question: Within what time frame must a work-related fatality be reported to OSHA?
questions.explanation: The passage specifies that 'any work-related fatality must be reported within eight hours,' while hospitalizations, amputations, or loss of an eye are reported within 24 hours.

questions.question: Which form is used to total the year's cases and must be posted in the workplace?
questions.explanation: The passage states the OSHA 300A Summary totals the year's cases and must be posted from February 1 through April 30.

questions.question: It can be inferred from the passage that an employer with eight employees in a low-hazard office setting would most likely:
choices: Be required to keep the OSHA 300 Log routinely
Be exempt from routine recordkeeping but still must report a fatality to OSHA
Be exempt from all OSHA reporting requirements entirely
Have to post the 300A Summary year-round
questions.explanation: Employers with ten or fewer employees are exempt from routine recordkeeping, but the passage stresses that 'all covered employers, regardless of size or industry, must still report the most severe events.' Combining both facts supports this inference.

questions.question: As used in the passage, the word 'recordable' most nearly means an injury or illness that:
choices: Must be entered into the required OSHA logs
questions.explanation: The passage defines a recordable case by criteria such as death, days away from work, or treatment beyond first aid, and these are the cases that go on the OSHA logs. In context, 'recordable' means it must be recorded.

questions.question: Which choice would make the BEST title for the passage?
choices: A Guide to Workers' Compensation Claims
How to Win an OSHA Citation Appeal
questions.explanation: The passage centers on the OSHA recordkeeping forms and posting requirements.

questions.question: All of the following are supported by the passage EXCEPT:
choices: Form 300A is the annual summary that must be posted
Some small employers are exempt from routine recordkeeping
First-aid-only cases are typically recordable on Form 300
Form 301 documents the details of a specific incident
questions.explanation: First-aid-only cases are generally NOT recordable; the passage distinguishes recordable injuries from first aid.

questions.question: Which sentence BEST summarizes the passage?
choices: Employers must post Form 301 in a public area year-round.
OSHA tracks workers' compensation premiums for every employer.
All first-aid cases must be logged on Form 300.
OSHA recordkeeping requires covered employers to log recordable injuries on Forms 300/301, post the 300A annual summary, with some small-employer exemptions.
questions.explanation: This captures the forms, the posting rule, and the exemption noted in the passage.

questions.question: What is 2/3 divided by 4?
questions.explanation: Dividing by 4 means multiplying by 1/4: (2/3) × (1/4) = 2/12 = 1/6. (8/3 multiplies by 4 instead; 1/12 divides 2/3 by 8 — too much; 3/8 inverts the wrong fraction.)
