questions.explanation: 100 divided by 5 is 20, times 2 is 40. (25 is 1/4; 20 is only 1/5; 50 is 1/2.)

questions.question: Two gears have a tooth ratio of 2:9. If the smaller gear has 10 teeth, how many teeth does the larger gear have?
questions.explanation: Scale factor = 10 / 2 = 5. Larger gear = 9 x 5 = 45 teeth.

questions.question: A square garden has sides of 7 meters each. What is its perimeter?
questions.explanation: Perimeter of a square = 4 × side = 4 × 7 = 28 m. Choice D (49) is the area; A (14) doubles instead of quadrupling.

questions.question: A triangle has sides of 6, 8, and 11 inches. What is its perimeter?
questions.explanation: Perimeter = sum of all sides = 6 + 8 + 11 = 25 in. Choice B (22) drops a side by miscounting; C (48) is nearly double.

questions.question: A worker recorded temperatures of 70, 74, and 78 degrees over three readings. What is the average?
questions.explanation: Average = (70 + 74 + 78) / 3 = 222 / 3 = 74 degrees. Choice D (222) is the sum without dividing.

questions.question: If 5 identical resistors cost $12, how much do 15 resistors cost?
questions.explanation: 15 is 3 times 5, so the cost triples: 12 x 3 = $36.

passages.title: Scaffolding Requirements
passages.text:
Scaffolds are temporary elevated platforms used to support workers and materials during construction, maintenance, or repair tasks. Because falls from scaffolds account for a significant share of jobsite injuries, OSHA 29 CFR 1926.451 governs how scaffolds must be designed, erected, and inspected. The foundation of any scaffold must be sound, rigid, and capable of carrying the intended load without settling or displacement. Footings or base plates rest on mudsills or other firm surfaces, never on unstable objects such as loose bricks, concrete blocks, or barrels.

Under 1926.451(a)(1), a scaffold and its components must support at least four times the maximum intended load. The maximum intended load includes the combined weight of workers, tools, and materials placed on the platform at any one time. This safety factor provides a margin against overloading, defective materials, and uneven weight distribution. Suspension ropes and their connecting hardware must support six times the intended load because they carry the platform without rigid support from below.

Platforms must be fully planked or decked between the front uprights and the guardrail supports. The gap between adjacent planks, or between a plank and the uprights, should not exceed one inch unless a wider space is required to fit around an upright. On a platform 10 feet or less in length, planks must extend over their end supports by at least 6 inches and not more than 12 inches; on longer platforms the maximum may be 18 inches when the plank is supported.

Under 1926.451(g)(1), fall protection — guardrail systems, personal fall arrest, or both depending on scaffold type — is required for workers on scaffolds MORE THAN 10 feet above a lower level. Guardrails consist of a top rail set approximately 42 inches above the platform (the standard allows 39 to 45 inches), a midrail roughly midway, and toeboards where there is danger of tools falling on people below. Access to scaffold platforms must be provided by ladders, stair towers, ramps, or built-in rungs; workers may not climb cross-bracing as a means of access.

A competent person must inspect the scaffold before each work shift and after any event that could affect its structural integrity, such as a storm or accidental impact. Damaged or weakened components must be repaired or replaced immediately, and the scaffold must be tagged out of service until safe.

passages.title: Personal Protective Equipment
passages.text:
Personal protective equipment, commonly abbreviated as PPE, refers to gear worn by workers to reduce exposure to hazards that can cause injury or illness. PPE is considered the last line of defense in workplace safety. Whenever possible, employers are expected first to eliminate or engineer out a hazard, then to control it through safe work practices, and only afterward to rely on PPE. This order matters because PPE protects a single worker at a time and only when it is worn correctly, whereas removing a hazard protects everyone.

Eye and face protection guards against flying particles, chemical splashes, and harmful light. Safety glasses with side shields handle most impact hazards and should meet the ANSI Z87.1 standard for industrial eye protection, while goggles seal against dust and liquids. A face shield protects the entire face but is treated as secondary protection and is worn over primary eyewear, not in place of it. Welding operations require filtered lenses rated to the appropriate shade number to block intense radiant energy.

Head protection comes from hard hats, which are divided into classes based on the electrical protection they provide. Class E helmets resist high-voltage exposure, Class G offers limited voltage protection, and Class C provides no electrical protection at all. A hard hat that has taken a heavy blow should be removed from service even if no damage is visible, because its ability to absorb a future impact may be compromised.

Hearing protection, such as earplugs or earmuffs, is required when noise exposure reaches OSHA's action level of 85 dB measured as an 8-hour time-weighted average (TWA); the permissible exposure limit (PEL) is 90 dB TWA. Each device carries a noise reduction rating (NRR) that estimates how much it lowers the sound reaching the ear. Respiratory protection ranges from simple filtering facepieces to supplied-air respirators, and the type selected must match the specific contaminant and its concentration. A tight-fitting respirator requires a fit test to confirm a proper seal, and facial hair that crosses the seal area can defeat that seal.

Hand protection must be matched to the task: cut-resistant gloves for sharp materials, insulated gloves for electrical work, and chemical-resistant gloves chosen by the substance handled. Foot protection includes safety-toe boots and, where needed, soles that resist puncture or slipping. Employers must train workers on when PPE is necessary, how to wear and adjust it, its limitations, and how to care for and dispose of it. Damaged equipment must be replaced, since worn or defective gear can give a false sense of security while offering little real protection.

passages.title: Underground Utility Locating
passages.text:
Before any excavation begins, contractors must identify the location of buried utilities to prevent damage, injury, and costly service interruptions. The process starts with a notification to a regional one-call center, often reached by dialing 811 in the United States. By law, the excavator must place this call a set number of business days before digging, giving utility owners time to respond. The one-call center forwards the request to every member utility whose lines may run through the work area.

Locators then visit the site to mark the approximate position of buried facilities using a standardized color code. White marks the proposed excavation area, red indicates electric power lines, yellow signals gas or other flammable material, orange shows communication and signal lines, blue denotes potable water, green marks sewer and drain lines, and purple identifies reclaimed water or slurry. These colors are recognized nationally, which reduces confusion when crews move between regions.

Locating itself relies on electromagnetic equipment. A transmitter applies a signal to a conductive line, and a handheld receiver detects the resulting field at the surface, allowing the locator to trace the line's path and estimate its depth. For non-conductive pipes, such as certain plastic gas or water mains, a tracer wire may have been buried alongside the pipe, or a flexible sonde can be pushed through the line to emit a locatable signal. Ground-penetrating radar offers another option, though its readings can be difficult to interpret in wet or clay-heavy soils.

Marks indicate only the approximate horizontal position, not the exact depth, so most regulations require hand digging or vacuum excavation within a defined tolerance zone on either side of a mark. This careful exposure of the line is sometimes called potholing or daylighting. Even with accurate locates, records can be incomplete, abandoned lines may remain in the ground, and soil movement can shift facilities over time.

Documentation closes the loop. Locators photograph and log their marks, and excavators are expected to preserve those marks throughout the project. If marks fade or are disturbed, a re-mark request must be submitted. Following these steps protects workers from electrocution and explosion hazards while shielding the public from the loss of essential services.

passages.title: Rigging and Load Handling
passages.text:
Rigging is the practice of attaching, securing, and controlling a load so it can be lifted and moved safely by a crane, hoist, or other lifting device. A successful lift depends less on the size of the crane than on careful planning by the people who connect the load. The worker responsible for this connection is the rigger, while a separate signal person often directs the crane operator, especially when the operator cannot see the load throughout its travel.

Every lift begins with knowing the weight of the load. If the weight is unknown, it must be calculated or obtained from documentation rather than guessed. The rigger then selects slings and hardware whose working load limit, or WLL, exceeds the demands of the lift. The WLL is the maximum force a component is rated to carry under normal conditions, and it already includes a safety factor below the point of failure. Exceeding the WLL is never acceptable, even briefly.

The angle at which a sling is loaded has a powerful effect on the tension it carries. As a sling angle drops away from vertical, the force in each leg rises sharply. A two-leg sling spread at a wide, shallow angle may carry far more tension per leg than the simple division of the load by two would suggest. Riggers consult angle charts so they do not unknowingly overload a sling that appears adequate.

The center of gravity also governs a lift. When the hook is positioned directly above the center of gravity, the load rises level and stable. If the rigging is off-center, the load tilts and may swing or slip, putting workers at risk. Tag lines, which are ropes held by ground crew, let workers steady and guide a suspended load without placing their hands beneath it.

Before the lift, all rigging must be inspected and any damaged sling removed from service. Frayed wire rope, cut synthetic webbing, cracked hooks, and missing safety latches are cause for rejection. During the lift, no one is permitted to stand or pass under a suspended load. These disciplines, applied consistently, keep both the load and the crew out of harm's way.

questions.question: In the figure, a ramp is 15 ft long and lifts a crate to a height of 3 ft. How many times does the ramp multiply the worker's effort?
questions.explanation: Mechanical advantage = length/height = 15/3 = 5, so the ramp multiplies effort 5 times.

questions.question: In the drawing, where is the fluid PRESSURE the highest?
choices: Pressure is the same at both openings
questions.explanation: In the wider section the fluid slows down, and slower fluid has higher pressure. Pressure is highest at the thick opening.

questions.question: Two identical bulbs are wired in series with a battery. How does the brightness of each bulb compare to a single bulb connected alone to the same battery?
choices: Each series bulb is dimmer than the single bulb
Each series bulb is brighter than the single bulb
questions.explanation: In series, the two bulbs share the battery voltage and the added resistance reduces the current. Each bulb gets less voltage and current than a lone bulb would, so each is dimmer.

questions.question: In the drawing, three gears are meshed in a row. The first gear (20 teeth) turns clockwise. Which way does the third gear (18 teeth) turn?
questions.explanation: In a row of meshed gears, direction alternates. Gear 1 clockwise, gear 2 counterclockwise, gear 3 clockwise. The middle gear is an idler, so the third gear matches the first.

questions.question: The figure shows a slab being pried up. Which single change would make the job EASIER?
choices: Using a longer bar and pushing at its end
Sliding the fulcrum away from the slab
Pushing down right above the fulcrum
questions.explanation: A longer bar pushed at the end lengthens the effort arm, reducing force. The other options shorten the effort arm or shift the fulcrum the wrong way.

questions.question: The drawing shows two setups for lifting the same 60 lb bucket: System X uses one fixed pulley, System Y uses one movable pulley. Which lets the worker lift the bucket with LESS force?
questions.explanation: A fixed pulley has MA = 1 (60 lb effort), while a movable pulley has MA = 2 (only 30 lb effort). The movable pulley, System Y, requires less force.

questions.question: Two springs in the figure each hold the same small motor. The short spring stretches only 2 cm while the long spring stretches 14 cm. Which spring is the softest (weakest)?
questions.explanation: Under equal loads, the spring that stretches the most is the softest. The long spring stretches 14 cm versus 2 cm, so it is the softest/weakest spring.

questions.question: In a parallel circuit with two bulbs, what happens to the total current the battery must supply compared with running just one bulb?
choices: The battery supplies more total current
The battery supplies less total current
The total current does not change
questions.explanation: Each parallel branch draws its own current from the battery. Adding a second branch means the battery must supply the combined current of both, so the total current increases.

questions.question: In the figure a 9 kg weight and a 36 kg weight are released together from the same height. Neglecting air resistance, what happens as they fall?
choices: They stay side by side and land together
The 36 kg weight pulls ahead and lands first
The 9 kg weight drifts ahead and lands first
questions.explanation: Both weights experience the same gravitational acceleration g, so they fall side by side and land at the same time. Mass has no effect on the rate of fall.

questions.question: The drawing shows a tiny 2 kg ball and a heavy 50 kg ball released from the same height at the same time. Ignoring air resistance, which ball wins the race to the floor?
questions.explanation: Even with a large mass difference, free-fall acceleration is identical for both balls. From the same height they land at the same time, so the race is a tie.

questions.question: The figure shows a boulder on one end of a lever. If you slide your hands inward toward the fulcrum while pushing down, what happens to the force you must apply?
questions.explanation: Sliding inward shortens the effort arm. A shorter effort arm requires more force, so you must push harder.

questions.question: The drawing shows a window-washer's platform raised by a single fixed pulley anchored to the roof, holding a 90 lb load. The force on the rope is:
questions.explanation: A fixed pulley gives no mechanical advantage (MA = 1); it only redirects the rope. Effort = 90 lb.

questions.question: In the drawing, a small piston of 2 square inches and a large piston of 10 square inches share the same oil. Which piston would you place a heavy car on to lift it with the least effort?
questions.explanation: The larger piston develops more force from the same pressure, since force equals pressure times area. The 10 sq in piston gives 5 times the force of the 2 sq in piston, so the car should sit on the large piston.

questions.question: The figure shows a ramp whose slope length and rise are both labeled 7 ft. What does this tell you about the ramp?
choices: It gives no force advantage (MA = 1), like lifting straight up
It gives a seven-times force advantage (MA = 7)
questions.explanation: MA = length/height = 7/7 = 1. When the slope length equals the height the ramp is essentially vertical and provides no mechanical advantage.

questions.question: In the figure, a 55 gallon drum is set exactly at the middle of a beam that rests on supports A and B. How is its weight shared?
choices: A and B each carry half
questions.explanation: The load sits midway, 7 ft from each support, so each support carries one half of the weight.

questions.question: Water flows through the pipe in the figure. Where does the water move FASTER?
choices: The speed is the same everywhere
questions.explanation: For a constant flow rate, the same volume must pass each second. Where the pipe is narrower, the water must speed up, so flow is faster at the narrow outlet.

questions.question: Based on the drawing, in which section is the flow EASIER to push a high speed through?
choices: The tight throat naturally forces higher speed
The open mouth naturally forces higher speed
Speed is unaffected by the pipe width
questions.explanation: To keep flow rate constant, fluid must move fastest where the pipe is narrowest. The tight throat naturally has the higher speed.

questions.question: The drawing shows a 50 cm pulley belted to a 25 cm pulley. The smaller pulley turns how fast compared to the larger one?
questions.explanation: Belt speed is inversely proportional to diameter. The 25 cm pulley is half the size of the 50 cm pulley, so it turns twice as fast.

questions.question: A wheel-and-axle has a wheel only slightly larger than the axle. The mechanical advantage is:
questions.explanation: Mechanical advantage is the ratio of radii; close radii give a ratio just above 1.

questions.question: In the drawing, four equal gears mesh in a row. The first turns clockwise. Which way does the fourth gear turn?
questions.explanation: Direction alternates along the train: gear 1 CW, gear 2 CCW, gear 3 CW, gear 4 CCW. The fourth gear turns counterclockwise.

questions.question: A piece of dry pine wood and a steel marble of equal volume are dropped into water at the same time. The pine floats and the steel sinks. The reason is:
choices: Steel is denser than water and pine is less dense than water
questions.explanation: An object floats if its density (mass per volume) is less than the surrounding fluid; sinks if greater. Pine ≈ 0.5 g/cm³, water = 1 g/cm³, steel ≈ 7.8 g/cm³.

questions.question: In the figure, the 9 cm pulley is the driver and the 27 cm pulley is driven by an open belt. The driven pulley turns:
choices: Three times slower than the driver
Three times faster than the driver
At the same speed as the driver
questions.explanation: Output speed is inversely proportional to diameter. The 27 cm pulley is three times the driver's 9 cm diameter, so it turns three times slower.

questions.question: A sealed plastic container holding only air floats easily on water; the same container packed with marbles sinks. What changed between the two cases?
choices: The temperature of the water shifted
The container's average density rose above that of water
questions.explanation: Adding heavy contents without changing the container's volume raises the AVERAGE density. When that density passes water's density (1 g/cm³), the object sinks.

questions.question: Two bulbs are wired in series across a battery. If a third identical bulb is added to the same series string, what happens to the brightness of the original bulbs?
questions.explanation: Adding another bulb in series increases the total resistance, which lowers the current. With less current, the same battery voltage is now split among three bulbs instead of two, so all of them get dimmer.

questions.question: Both surfaces are very slick. Which statement best describes pushing a box across either one?
choices: Both require very little force because friction is low
Ice always requires more force than oil
Oil always requires more force than ice
questions.explanation: Both ice and oiled steel have very low friction, so only a small force is needed.

questions.question: A locksmith taps a thin metal shim between a door and its frame. Even a small hammer tap creates a strong binding force because:
choices: The shim acts as a wedge that converts a small driving force into a large normal force
The shim removes the friction between the door and frame
The hammer adds mass to the lock mechanism
questions.explanation: A thin wedge has a very high mechanical advantage: a small force driving it forward becomes a much larger force pushing the surfaces apart.

questions.question: A hand winch turns a long handle to wind a rope onto a small drum. This is a wheel-and-axle because:
choices: The long handle acts as a large wheel, the drum as the axle
The handle reduces the load's weight
questions.explanation: The handle's long radius and small drum radius multiply the operator's force into the rope tension.

questions.question: The figure shows two hydraulic cylinders connected by a pipe. The left piston is 7 square inches and the right piston is 21 square inches. If both are pressed by the same fluid, which exerts MORE force?
choices: Neither, force does not depend on area
questions.explanation: Force depends directly on area when pressure is held equal by the fluid. The 21 sq in piston has 3 times the area of the 7 sq in piston and therefore exerts 3 times the force.

questions.question: Two scuba divers are at the same 40-ft depth in a connected harbor, but one is near the shore and one is near a deeper trench far away. The water pressure on each diver is:
choices: Greater on the diver near the deeper trench
Greater on the diver near shore
questions.explanation: Pressure in a connected static fluid depends only on depth, not on the surrounding container's shape or distance. Same depth → same pressure.

questions.question: An underwater storage tank is built with thicker steel walls near the bottom than at the top. The main reason is:
choices: Steel weakens with depth in cold water
The base is more difficult to weld
Water pressure increases with depth, so the bottom faces a greater outward force
questions.explanation: Hydrostatic pressure equals ρ·g·h. The deeper the wall, the higher the pressure pushing outward, so more material is needed to resist it.

questions.question: The figure shows a water tank on a beam, sitting a bit left of center between supports A and B. Which support takes slightly more of the weight?
questions.explanation: The tank is 6 ft from A and 9 ft from B. Because it is nearer A, support A takes the slightly larger share. Reaction at A = 9/15 = 60 percent.

questions.question: Two carts are at rest. Cart A weighs 50 lb and cart B weighs 500 lb. Which is harder to start moving?
questions.explanation: Greater mass means greater inertia, so the heavier cart resists changes in motion more strongly.

questions.question: A dockworker rigs a single movable pulley to lift a 400 N crate of fish off the deck. Ignoring friction, how much rope force is needed?
questions.explanation: A single movable pulley gives MA = 2, so the required pull is half the load: 400 N ÷ 2 = 200 N.

questions.question: The figure shows one spring holding a single weight, stretching 6 cm. If a second identical weight is added so two equal weights now hang, what happens to the stretch shown in the drawing?
choices: The stretch is cut in half to about 3 cm
The stretch doubles to about 12 cm
questions.explanation: Stretch is proportional to the load on a given spring. Doubling the hanging weight roughly doubles the stretch, so 6 cm becomes about 12 cm.

questions.question: In the figure, a tiny 9-tooth gear meshes with a 45-tooth gear. Which gear completes more revolutions in one minute?
questions.explanation: Fewer teeth means faster rotation. The 9-tooth gear makes 5 turns for each turn of the 45-tooth gear, so it completes more revolutions.

questions.question: A loaded truck and an empty truck travel at the same speed. Which is harder to bring to a stop?
questions.explanation: More mass means more inertia, so the loaded truck resists stopping more.

questions.question: In the drawing, two ramps reach the same 4 ft loading dock: Ramp A is 8 ft long and Ramp B is 16 ft long. Using which ramp requires LESS pushing force to roll a barrel up?
choices: Both require exactly the same force
questions.explanation: A longer, gentler ramp to the same height gives greater mechanical advantage (16/4 = 4 vs 8/4 = 2), so the longer Ramp B needs less force.

questions.question: In the drawing, the effort is applied closer to the fulcrum than the stone is. How does the required effort compare to the stone's weight?
choices: The effort must be larger than the stone's weight
The effort must be smaller than the stone's weight
The effort equals the stone's weight
questions.explanation: The effort arm is shorter than the load arm, so this lever increases the force needed. The effort must exceed the stone's weight.

questions.question: Two wedges are driven the same distance into a log. The wide wedge, compared to the narrow one:
choices: Spreads the wood more per stroke but requires more force per stroke
questions.explanation: A wider wedge spreads more per stroke but offers less mechanical advantage, requiring more force.

questions.question: In the figure, two cars start side by side and drive around a bend in the road, staying in their lanes the whole way. The dark car hugs the inside edge of the curve while the light car rides the outside edge. If both reach the end of the bend at the same instant, which car had to travel faster?
choices: Neither, because cars in adjacent lanes always move at the same speed
The inside (dark) car, because the inside lane is the more direct route
The outside (light) car, because its lane traces a longer path around the curve
questions.explanation: On a curve the outer lane is a larger arc than the inner lane. To cover that longer path in the same amount of time, the outside car must move faster than the inside car.

questions.question: At the surface of a swimming pool, water pressure due to the water column is:
questions.explanation: At the water surface, the depth is zero so pressure from the water column is essentially zero.

questions.question: A logger has two axes — one with a very steep (thin) blade angle and one with a wider blade. Compared with the wider blade, the narrower-angle axe:
choices: Needs less force per swing but more swings to split a log
Needs more force per swing but fewer swings
Behaves identically to the wider blade
questions.explanation: A narrower wedge has higher mechanical advantage (force in × distance in = force out × distance out). Lower force per swing but each swing advances less, so more swings total.

questions.question: Hydraulic fluid enters the small left end and exits the large right end. Which end shows higher fluid speed?
questions.explanation: Smaller cross-section means higher velocity. The left (narrow) end has greater speed than the wide right end.

questions.question: The drawing shows a crate being lifted with a lever. If the fulcrum is moved closer to the crate, what happens to the effort needed?
questions.explanation: Moving the fulcrum nearer the load shortens the load arm and lengthens the effort arm, making the lift easier. Less effort is needed.

questions.question: What is the main idea of the passage?
choices: Scaffolds are the most expensive equipment on a construction site
Suspension ropes are the only part of a scaffold that can fail
Most construction workers prefer scaffolds over ladders
Regulations govern how scaffolds must be built, loaded, accessed, and inspected to prevent injuries
questions.explanation: The passage as a whole explains the rules covering scaffold design, loading, access, and inspection, all aimed at preventing falls and collapse. The other options are narrow details or claims not supported by the text.

questions.question: According to the passage, a scaffold and its components must support at least how many times the maximum intended load?
questions.explanation: The passage states the general rule that a scaffold and its components must support at least four times the maximum intended load. Six times applies specifically to suspension ropes.

questions.question: Why must suspension ropes support six times the intended load rather than four?
choices: Because ropes are cheaper than rigid supports
Because they carry the platform without rigid support from below
Because they are inspected less often
Because they are always made of steel
questions.explanation: The passage explains that suspension ropes and their hardware must support six times the load because they carry the platform without rigid support from below, requiring a larger safety margin.

questions.question: As used in the passage, the word "competent" most nearly means:
questions.explanation: The passage defines a competent person as someone capable of identifying hazards and authorized to take prompt corrective action, so 'competent' here means capable and authorized to act.

questions.question: It can be inferred from the passage that resting scaffold footings on loose bricks or barrels is prohibited because:
choices: Bricks and barrels are too expensive to use
Such objects are unstable and could shift or settle under load
They make the scaffold harder to climb
questions.explanation: The passage requires a sound, rigid foundation and specifically forbids unstable objects. The inference is that loose bricks or barrels could shift or settle, undermining the scaffold's stability.

questions.question: Which choice would make the BEST title for the passage?
choices: Safe Scaffolding: Capacity, Guardrails, Access, and Inspection
questions.explanation: The passage covers capacity (4x), guardrails, planking, access, and competent-person inspection — all scaffolding essentials.

questions.question: According to the passage, which step must occur BEFORE workers use a scaffold each shift?
choices: Increasing the load to 5x the design capacity
questions.explanation: A competent person must inspect the scaffold before use.

questions.question: All of the following are supported by the passage EXCEPT:
choices: Scaffolds must be capable of supporting four times the intended load
Fall protection is required for workers more than 10 feet above a lower level
Access should be provided by ladder or stair
Workers may climb the cross-bracing as the normal means of access
questions.explanation: The passage explicitly says workers may NOT climb cross-bracing for access (ladders, stairs, ramps, or rungs are required), so D is contradicted. The other three statements are directly supported: 4× load capacity (A), the >10-ft fall-protection trigger (B), and the access methods (C).

questions.question: What is the central idea of the passage?
choices: PPE is the first and best method of controlling workplace hazards
Different types of PPE protect against different hazards and must be selected, worn, and maintained correctly
Hard hats are the only PPE required on a jobsite
Employers are not responsible for training workers on PPE
questions.explanation: The passage describes various categories of PPE and stresses correct selection, use, and maintenance. It explicitly states PPE is the last line of defense, not the first, ruling out the other options.

questions.question: According to the passage, where does PPE rank among methods of controlling hazards?
choices: It is the first method employers should use
It is the last line of defense, used after eliminating or controlling hazards
It is equal in priority to engineering controls
questions.explanation: The passage states PPE is considered the last line of defense and that employers should first eliminate or engineer out hazards and then control them before relying on PPE.

questions.question: Which class of hard hat provides NO electrical protection?
questions.explanation: The passage states that Class C provides no electrical protection at all, while Class E resists high voltage and Class G offers limited voltage protection.

questions.question: As used in the passage, the phrase "false sense of security" most nearly means:
choices: A correct belief that one is safe
A mistaken belief of being protected when one is not
A feeling of fear about the job
questions.explanation: The passage warns that worn or defective gear can give a false sense of security while offering little real protection, meaning a mistaken belief of being protected when one actually is not.

questions.question: It can be inferred from the passage that a hard hat which has absorbed a heavy blow should be replaced even with no visible damage because:
choices: It will look unprofessional to coworkers
Its ability to absorb a future impact may be reduced
It will no longer fit the worker's head
It automatically loses its class rating
questions.explanation: The passage says such a hard hat should be removed from service because its ability to absorb a future impact may be compromised, supporting the inference about reduced future protection.

questions.question: Which choice would make the BEST title for the passage?
choices: PPE Basics: Head, Eyes, Ears, Hands, and Feet
questions.explanation: The passage walks through hard hats, ANSI eyewear, hearing protection, gloves, and footwear.

questions.question: According to the passage, what triggers the requirement to provide hearing protection?
choices: A noise exposure at or above an 85 dB time-weighted average
Only the use of compressed air
questions.explanation: The passage states OSHA's action level for hearing protection is 85 dB measured as an 8-hour time-weighted average. (The PEL of 90 dB is also mentioned but the action level — when hearing protection must be provided and a hearing-conservation program begun — is 85 dB.)

questions.question: All of the following are supported by the passage EXCEPT:
choices: Safety glasses should meet ANSI Z87.1
Hard hats come in different classes for electrical hazards
Gloves should be chosen based on the hazard
One pair of leather gloves is appropriate for every hazard, including chemicals
questions.explanation: Glove selection must match the hazard; one pair does not fit all. The other three claims are now directly supported by the passage: A (safety glasses should meet ANSI Z87.1), B (hard hat classes E/G/C), C (gloves chosen by task / hazard).

questions.question: What is the main idea of the passage?
choices: Ground-penetrating radar is the most reliable locating method available
A systematic locating process protects workers and the public before excavation
The color code was designed mainly to help crews working in multiple regions
One-call centers are responsible for performing all utility excavation
questions.explanation: The passage as a whole describes the steps of locating buried utilities and states they protect workers and the public, making this the central idea. The other choices reference details that are subordinate or contradicted by the text.

questions.question: According to the passage, what color is used to mark gas or other flammable material?
questions.explanation: The passage states directly that yellow signals gas or other flammable material. Red marks electric power, orange marks communication lines, and green marks sewer and drain lines.

questions.question: Based on the passage, why is hand digging or vacuum excavation required near a mark?
choices: Because marks show only approximate horizontal position and not exact depth
Because electromagnetic equipment cannot be used near buried lines
Because the one-call center requires it before forwarding a request
Because color codes vary too much between regions to trust
questions.explanation: This is an inference supported by the statement that marks indicate only approximate horizontal position, not exact depth, which is why careful exposure within a tolerance zone is required. The other options are not supported by the passage.

questions.question: As used in the passage, the word "sonde" most nearly refers to
choices: A type of tracer wire buried alongside a pipe
A device pushed through a line to emit a locatable signal
A handheld receiver that detects electromagnetic fields
questions.explanation: The passage describes a flexible sonde that can be pushed through the line to emit a locatable signal. The other choices describe different tools or entities mentioned in the text.

questions.question: Why does the author most likely include the detail that abandoned lines may remain in the ground and soil can shift facilities?
choices: To argue that one-call centers are unnecessary
To show that even accurate locates have limitations
To explain how the color code was developed
To prove that plastic pipes are safer than metal pipes
questions.explanation: This is an author's-purpose question. The detail follows the statement 'Even with accurate locates' and serves to show locating has limits, reinforcing the need for caution. The other choices misrepresent the author's intent.

questions.question: According to the passage, place these actions in the correct order from first to last: (1) hand-dig within the tolerance zone, (2) call 811, (3) observe the colored marks left by locators.
questions.explanation: Call 811 first; locators then leave color-coded marks; only then hand-dig within the tolerance zone.

questions.question: Based on the passage, the most likely consequence of using a mechanical excavator inside the tolerance zone would be:
choices: Striking and damaging a marked underground utility
Receiving a refund of the 811 locating fee
Having the survey marks repainted in pink
Extending the tolerance zone to 36 inches
questions.explanation: Within the locally defined tolerance zone, the passage requires hand-digging or vacuum excavation because marks are only approximate. Using a mechanical excavator there risks striking the marked utility. The other answers are unrelated to that risk.

questions.question: Which color and utility pairing is NOT supported by the passage?
questions.explanation: Per the passage, purple is used for reclaimed water or slurry, not for steam — so D is unsupported. The supported color/utility pairings in the passage include red/electric, yellow/gas, orange/communications, blue/potable water, green/sewer, white/proposed dig, and purple/reclaimed water.

questions.question: What is the central idea of the passage?
choices: Cranes fail more often than the slings attached to them
Safe load handling depends on careful rigging practices rather than crane size
Signal persons are more important than riggers on every job
Tag lines have replaced the need to know a load's weight
questions.explanation: The passage opens by stating a successful lift depends on careful planning by those connecting the load, not crane size, and the rest develops safe rigging practices. The other choices overstate or contradict the text.

questions.question: According to the passage, what does WLL stand for and represent?
choices: Working load limit, the maximum force a component is rated to carry
Weighted lift level, the average weight of all loads in a day
Wire line length, the total length of a sling
Wide lift latitude, the allowable swing of a suspended load
questions.explanation: The passage defines WLL as working load limit and describes it as the maximum force a component is rated to carry under normal conditions. The other choices are invented and unsupported.

questions.question: Based on the passage, what happens to the tension in each sling leg as the sling angle becomes shallower?
choices: The tension stays the same regardless of angle
The tension only changes if the load is unknown
questions.explanation: This is an inference from the statement that as a sling angle drops away from vertical, the force in each leg rises sharply. The other choices contradict the passage.

questions.question: As used in the passage, the phrase "center of gravity" most nearly refers to
choices: The heaviest single sling in the rigging assembly
The midpoint of the crane's boom
The location of the signal person on the ground
The point about which the load's weight is balanced
questions.explanation: The passage explains that when the hook is above the center of gravity the load rises level and stable, indicating it is the balance point of the load. The other choices misidentify the term.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a tag line, according to the passage?
choices: To measure the working load limit of a sling
To calculate the weight of an unknown load
To attach the load directly to the crane hook
To let workers steady and guide a load without standing beneath it
questions.explanation: The passage states tag lines are ropes that let workers steady and guide a suspended load without placing their hands beneath it. The other choices describe unrelated functions.

questions.question: Which choice would make the BEST title for the passage?
choices: A History of the Mobile Crane
Rigging Fundamentals: Slings, Angles, Capacity, and Control
questions.explanation: The passage covers sling angles, capacity tags, inspection, center of gravity, and tag lines.

questions.question: According to the passage, what is the direct consequence of reducing the sling angle from the horizontal?
choices: The capacity of the sling increases
The center of gravity moves upward
The tension in each sling leg increases and effective capacity decreases
questions.explanation: As sling angle decreases, leg tension rises sharply and the assembly's effective capacity falls.

questions.question: With which statement would the author most likely agree?
choices: Tag lines should be avoided because they slow the lift
A qualified rigger should plan the lift and verify capacities
Capacity tags can be ignored if the load looks light
Center of gravity does not matter for symmetric loads
questions.explanation: The passage emphasizes the role of a qualified rigger in planning and verifying lifts.

questions.question: 15 is what percent of 60?
questions.explanation: 15 divided by 60 = 0.25 = 25%. (15% just repeats the number; 40% reverses the ratio; 4% divides wrong.)

questions.question: What is 3/4 of 60?
questions.explanation: 60 divided by 4 is 15, times 3 is 45. (15 is just 1/4; 20 is 1/3; 80 multiplies instead of taking a part.)

questions.question: What is 5/8 expressed as a decimal?
questions.explanation: 5 divided by 8 = 0.625. (0.58 just reads the digits; 1.6 divides 8 by 5; 0.8 estimates loosely.)

questions.question: A solution mixes acid to water in a 3:7 ratio. What fraction of the total solution is acid?
questions.explanation: Total parts = 3 + 7 = 10. Acid = 3 of 10 = 3/10. (3/7 ignores that the ratio parts must be added for the whole.)

questions.question: Over four shifts a machine produced 40, 50, 60, and 50 units. What is the average output per shift?
questions.explanation: Average = (40 + 50 + 60 + 50) / 4 = 200 / 4 = 50 units. Choice C (200) is the total without dividing.

questions.question: A triangle has a base of 10 cm and a height of 6 cm. What is its area?
questions.explanation: Area of a triangle = (1/2) × base × height = (1/2) × 10 × 6 = 30 sq cm. Choice A (60) forgets to halve.

questions.question: A rectangular field has a perimeter of 40 feet. If its width is 8 feet, what is its length?
questions.explanation: Perimeter = 2(L + W), so 40 = 2(L + 8). Then L + 8 = 20, giving L = 12 ft. Choice C (32) subtracts 8 from 40 directly.

questions.question: Five boxes weigh 12, 14, 16, 18, and 20 pounds. What is the average weight?
questions.explanation: Average = (12 + 14 + 16 + 18 + 20) / 5 = 80 / 5 = 16 lb. Choice C (80) is the total without dividing.

questions.question: Express 50 inches in feet and inches.
questions.explanation: 50 ÷ 12 = 4 with remainder 2, so 50 inches = 4 feet 2 inches.

questions.question: What is 4.5 divided by 0.9?
questions.explanation: Multiply both by 10: 45 divided by 9 = 5. (0.5 and 50 misplace the decimal; 4.05 multiplies instead of divides.)

questions.question: What is 1 divided by 0.25?
questions.explanation: 0.25 is 1/4, and there are four quarters in 1, so the answer is 4. (0.25 repeats the divisor; 0.4 and 2.5 misplace decimals.)

questions.question: A board is 4 yards long. What is its length in feet?
questions.explanation: 1 yard = 3 feet, so 4 × 3 = 12 feet.

questions.question: A crew of electricians to laborers is in the ratio 3:5. If there are 24 workers in total, how many are laborers?
questions.explanation: The ratio 3:5 has 8 parts. 24 / 8 = 3 per part. Laborers = 5 x 3 = 15. (9 is the count of electricians, a common mix-up.)

questions.question: If 4 pumps fill a tank in the same time using 60 gallons, how many gallons would 6 pumps move in that same time at the same rate?
questions.explanation: Gallons scale with pumps: 60 / 4 = 15 gallons per pump. 6 x 15 = 90 gallons.

questions.question: A motor turns 450 revolutions in 3 minutes. At that rate, how many revolutions does it make in 5 minutes?
questions.explanation: Rate = 450 / 3 = 150 rev per minute. 150 x 5 = 750 revolutions.

questions.question: A map uses a scale where 2 inches represents 50 miles. How many miles do 7 inches represent?
questions.explanation: 50 / 2 = 25 miles per inch. 7 x 25 = 175 miles.

questions.question: A worker assembles 8 units every 20 minutes. How many units are assembled in 2 hours?
questions.explanation: In 20 minutes = 8 units, so per hour = 24 units (8 x 3). Two hours = 48 units.

questions.question: Concrete is mixed with cement to sand in a 1:4 ratio. If 8 bags of cement are used, how many bags of sand are needed?
questions.explanation: Sand is 4 times the cement: 4 x 8 = 32 bags.

questions.question: The figure shows a right-triangular brace with its two legs dimensioned. How long is the diagonal brace?
questions.explanation: Hypotenuse = sqrt(12^2 + 16^2) = 20 ft.

questions.question: The figure shows a scaled drawing. At the scale indicated, what is the actual length represented by the dimension on the plan?
questions.explanation: 3.5 in x 20 ft per in = 70 ft.

questions.question: According to the bar chart in the figure, what is the largest single value shown?
questions.explanation: Read the bars and compute: 9.

questions.question: According to the table in the figure, what is the highest load value listed?
questions.explanation: From the table: 49.

questions.question: The figure shows a box with its edge lengths labeled. What is its volume?
questions.explanation: Volume = 4 x 2 x 3 = 24 cu ft.

questions.question: The figure shows a rectangular area with its sides dimensioned. What is its area?
questions.explanation: Area = 11 x 8 = 88 sq ft.

questions.question: Using the dimensions on the floor plan, what is the TOTAL floor area of the building?
questions.explanation: Read room dimensions from the plan and compute: 378 sq ft.

questions.question: According to the materials table, how many units of Drywall are needed?
questions.explanation: Read directly from the table: 23.

questions.question: Based on the floor plan in the figure, what is the TOTAL floor area of all three rooms?
questions.explanation: Multiply length x width: 324 sq ft.

questions.question: The elevation drawing shows a building. If the building's footprint is 25 ft by 15 ft, what is its TOTAL volume?
questions.explanation: Total volume = footprint area × total building height. Per the drawing, total height stacks the elevation segments shown: total height = 12750 / (25 × 15) = 34 ft. So volume = 25 × 15 × 34 = 12,750 cu ft.

questions.question: In the figure, a steel plate has 4 holes dimensioned in a chain. What is the center-to-center distance from Hole 1 to Hole 3 (dimension A)?
questions.explanation: Add the dimensions that span the requested distance: 5.75 in.

questions.question: In the figure, an L-shaped floor has a corner notch. Using the dimensions shown, what is the length of the unlabeled wall X?
questions.explanation: Subtract along the dimension: 9 ft.

questions.question: The figure shows a pipe run split into sections with the overall length given. What is the length of the missing section X?
questions.explanation: Subtract the known sections from the total: 4 ft.

questions.question: The figure shows a wall panel with a rectangular opening. What is the shaded (net) area of the panel?
questions.explanation: Panel minus opening: 16x7 - 7x3 = 91 sq ft.

questions.question: The figure shows a right-triangular brace with its two legs dimensioned. How long is the diagonal brace?
questions.explanation: Hypotenuse = sqrt(20^2 + 21^2) = 29 ft.

questions.question: The figure shows a scaled drawing. At the scale indicated, what is the actual length represented by the dimension on the plan?
questions.explanation: 5 in x 10 ft per in = 50 ft.
